summary: Black Rock Lighthouse on the Minas Channel, Kings County, has shown a light since 1848. Its present fibreglass tower dates from 1967 and is owned by the Coast Guard.

access.note: Canadian Coast Guard property. Grounds open, tower closed (Lighthouse Friends). A circular turnaround lies just past the light at the end of a gravel road.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Coast Guard list gives a focal height of 15.9 m (52 ft) above water. The NSLPS gives a light height of 49 ft (about 15 m). The story states the Coast Guard figure and gives the NSLPS figure as a little lower.

The record notes disagreeing first years. The 1848 date for this light is given by Lighthouse Friends and the NSLPS. The 1867 Board of Works contract that Lighthouse Friends prints for a first Black Rock light is for Black Rock Point in Cape Breton, a different station with the same name, and is not used.

notes_for_editor: 1) Wrong Black Rock avoided. Lighthouse Friends ID 1399 and the Department's keepers' tables under Black Rock Point (keeper M. D. Morrison) are Black Rock Point, Cape Breton, not this Kings County light. The 1867 Board of Works contract, and the 'Black Rock Point' keeper rows, are not used for this station. Likely source of the record's 'different first years' conflict. 2) Band count disagrees: the Coast Guard list gives one red horizontal band; Lighthouse Friends and the NSLPS give two. The story states both. 3) The NSLPS history note '1883 - catatropic light, fixed white, 12m, listed as Black Rock Point' is not used; it sits under the Black Rock I entry but names Black Rock Point, so it may belong to the other station. 4) Crotty (1848 to 1872) and James Robinson (1872 to 1885) rest on Lighthouse Friends alone; the corpus has no Canadian report before 1900. 5) The 1910 and 1912 keepers' tables were matched by column position (station then keeper): Charles Robinson sits between Black Rock and Black Rock Point; the checker should read the page images at scan page 166 (1910 volume) and scan page 242 (1912 volume). 6) Staffing 'automated by 1973' is the NSLPS history note for the station; the NSLPS's general line for Nova Scotia lights says 'automated by 1993'. 7) No Canadian newspaper search run (newspapers.py covers US papers). Thin: the story has no headings for that reason. 8) Fact-check 2026-10-28: the 1912 table line-pairs 'Black Rock Chas. Robinson' and 'Black Rock Point M. D. Morrison', and Lighthouse Friends gives Malcolm D. Morrison (1892 to 1929) at Black Rock Point, so the 1910 date for Charles Robinson (Mar. 16, 1885) sits with Black Rock by column position and is consistent with that adjacency. The archive.org page images (scan pages 166 and 242) could not be opened from the browser pane (access denied), so the 1910 date is checked against the OCR only. 9) The NSLPS light height (49 ft, about 15 m) differs slightly from the Coast Guard focal height (15.9 m); the story states both.
